over the DTLS record + framing layers, reusing the TLS 1.3 messages + key schedule. A minimal
in-test DTLS client completes the handshake end to end - deprotecting the server flight, verifying
the CertificateVerify signature and Finished MAC over the real transcript, and confirming both
sides install identical application-traffic keys. Also drives the HelloRetryRequest group
renegotiation (sec 5.1): a ClientHello with no X25519 key_share draws an HRR + address-bound cookie,
and the retry that echoes it completes over the message_hash || HRR || ClientHello2 transcript; a
retry without the cookie is rejected. An RFC 7250 Raw Public Keys case (PC_ENABLE_TLS_RPK) offers
server_certificate_type = RawPublicKey and confirms the server answers with a 44-byte Ed25519
SubjectPublicKeyInfo whose key CertificateVerify signs. Pure host tests.

native_coaps.desc:
CoAP over DTLS (services/iot/coap/coaps, RFC 7252 sec 9): the bridge that drives a DtlsConn
handshake and, once established, unwraps each epoch-3 application record, answers it with
coap_server_process(), and re-wraps the response. An in-test DTLS 1.3 client completes the handshake
and exchanges a CoAP GET, decrypting the CoAP response from the returned DTLS record; a replayed
application record is dropped. Pure host tests.

native_coaps_server.desc:
CoAP-over-DTLS server front-end (services/iot/coap/coaps_server): the per-peer DtlsConn pool +
ingest/poll seam on top of pc_coaps_process(). An in-test DTLS 1.3 client drives the server only through
coaps_server_ingest() and an output sink, exercising peer-address routing, the handshake + CoAP
exchange, the poll-driven retransmission timer (RFC 9147 sec 5.8), and idle-connection reaping. Two
simultaneous peers are routed to their own connections. Pure host tests.

native_tls13_kdf.desc:
TLS 1.3 key schedule for the QUIC handshake (network_drivers/tls/tls13_kdf,
RFC 8446 sec 7.1 / 4.4.4): Early/Handshake/Master secret Extract chain, client/server handshake +
application traffic secrets, the server handshake write key/iv label path, and the server Finished
verify_data over a full ClientHello..CertificateVerify transcript. Pinned to RFC 8448 sec 3.

native_quic_tp.desc:
QUIC transport parameters codec (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_tp, RFC 9000
sec 18): the sec 18.2 defaults, an encode/parse round-trip over the connection IDs + every varint
parameter + the migration flag, parsing a hand-built byte string, skipping unknown/GREASE ids, and
rejecting a duplicate parameter, an oversized connection ID, and out-of-range values.

native_tls13_msg.desc:
TLS 1.3 handshake messages for the QUIC handshake (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/
tls13_msg, RFC 8446 sec 4): ClientHello parse (X25519 key_share + capability flags), and the server
flight. Byte-exact vs RFC 8448 sec 3 for ServerHello / Certificate / Finished, plus the ALPN + QUIC
transport-params EncryptedExtensions and an Ed25519 CertificateVerify sign/verify round-trip.

native_quic_tls.desc:
TLS 1.3 server handshake state machine for QUIC (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/
quic_tls, RFC 9001 / RFC 8446): a full interop round-trip - drive the server with a hand-built
ClientHello, run the client half of the key schedule independently, and confirm both sides derive
identical handshake + application secrets and the server accepts the client Finished. Plus
capability-negotiation rejections (no h3 ALPN, bad Finished) and partial-CRYPTO handling.

native_quic_tls_pqc.desc:
TLS 1.3 QUIC handshake with the X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum hybrid group (IANA 0x11ec,
PC_ENABLE_PQC_KEX=1): drives the server with a hybrid ClientHello, then verifies it as a conforming
client - ML-KEM Decaps (an independent reference) + X25519, the 64-byte ML-KEM||X25519 secret, and
both Finished MACs. Reuses the classical test_quic_tls suite plus the added hybrid round-trip.

native_quic_conn.desc:
QUIC v1 server connection engine (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_conn, RFC 9000
/ RFC 9001): the test acts as a QUIC client - builds real Initial / Handshake / 1-RTT packets and
drives a server QuicConn through a full handshake (per-level AEAD, CRYPTO reassembly, ACKs,
coalescing, HANDSHAKE_DONE) and a 1-RTT request/response stream exchange.

native_h3_conn.desc:
HTTP/3 application engine (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/h3_conn, RFC 9114): drives
h3_conn through the quic_conn callback seam - a QPACK-encoded request on a request stream dispatches
the right method/path (+ a POST body), the control stream sends SETTINGS on handshake completion,
and a response (HEADERS + DATA) round-trips through the QUIC stream send buffer.

native_h3_e2e.desc:
End-to-end HTTP/3 capstone (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3): a QUIC client in the
test completes the TLS 1.3 handshake against a quic_conn + h3_conn server, sends a real HTTP/3 GET
(QPACK HEADERS in a STREAM frame), and verifies the app-served response (HEADERS :status 200 + DATA
body) - the whole stack composed: QUIC crypto/framing, TLS 1.3, streams, HTTP/3 framing, QPACK.

native_quic_server.desc:
HTTP/3 server glue (network_drivers/presentation/http/http3/quic_server): the UDP-facing pool
that routes datagrams by Destination Connection ID to a pool of QuicConn + H3Conn engines. A QUIC
client in the test injects datagrams through the host ingest seam and captures the server's replies
through the output sink, driving a full handshake + HTTP/3 GET and verifying the 200 + body - the
same end-to-end flow as test_h3_e2e but through pc_quic_server_begin / poll / respond, exercising the
connection-ID routing, the ingest ring, and new-connection creation from a client Initial.

native_h3_server.desc:
HTTP/3 dispatch bridge end-to-end through PC (the full Layer-7 app built with
PC_ENABLE_HTTP3=1): a QUIC client completes the handshake and sends an HTTP/3 GET, quic_server
routes it to the reserved dispatch slot, match_and_execute runs the registered route, and the
handler's send() is routed back onto the request stream via pc_quic_server_respond. Verifies the whole
wire: a real route handler answers an HTTP/3 request. Reuses the native_stack_http full-app base.

native_ssh_chachapoly.desc:
chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com AEAD (network_drivers/presentation/ssh): ChaCha20 vs RFC
8439 sec 2.3.2 block vector, Poly1305 vs RFC 8439 sec 2.5.2, and the OpenSSH construction
(length decode, encrypt/decrypt round-trip, tag-tamper + wrong-seqnr rejection). Pure host crypto.

native_ssh_aesgcm.desc:
AES-256-GCM AEAD for aes256-gcm@openssh.com (RFC 5647) host-tested here: seal/open vs the
NIST/McGrew AES-256-GCM Test Case 16 vector, tamper rejection, and the invocation-counter
advance. Software AES-256 + GHASH; no heap, no stdlib.

native_ssh_ecdsa.desc:
ECDSA P-256 for ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 (RFC 5656) host-tested on the software path: pubkey,
deterministic sign, and verify pinned byte-exact to the RFC 6979 A.2.5 (P-256/SHA-256)
vectors, plus tamper rejection. Self-contained field/point math + RFC 6979 (HMAC-SHA256).

native_frame.desc:
The declarative frame builder (shared_primitives/frame.h + frame.cpp): the single engine that
turns a static pc_field spec into wire bytes, so the ~160 formatting sites in this library carry
a table rather than a hand-written append sequence. Covers every field kind and width, the
fail-closed contract at the exact byte boundary (a frame that does not fit reports 0 AND leaves a
valid empty string, which is what a length comparison against snprintf's would-be length silently
got wrong), the append rewind that keeps a header line whole-or-absent, NULL string handling, and
a differential check of the numeric and float conversions against the libc printf whose output
these frames replace byte for byte.

native_span.desc:
The bounded byte region (server/mmgr/span.h): a pointer and the capacity that belongs to
it, bound together. Rule 19 converts stack arrays - whose length the compiler ties to the object -
into borrowed regions, and the naive rewrite to a bare pointer plus a separate cap argument is
where a 4-byte sizeof() or a mismatched capacity slips through with no diagnostic. Covers the
extent recovered from the array type, the normalization that makes {nullptr, n} unconstructible
so an omitted check writes nothing instead of dereferencing null, and the sub-span clamping that
keeps a truncated frame from producing a pointer past the allocation.

native_secure_pool.desc:
The secure pool accessor (server/mmgr/secure): the SAME pool mechanism as the plaintext side
(server/mmgr/arena) instantiated a second time at a disjoint address, so only what differs is
covered here - the access and control layer. Reclaiming WIPES, and wipes before the bytes become
available again, so a secret cannot survive its borrow or reach the next tenant; the scope guard
makes that hold on the early-return paths a hand-written wipe gets forgotten on. And the two
pools being disjoint regions means ownership is decided by address alone - a secure pointer can
never be accepted where a plaintext one is required, or the reverse, with no per-allocation
metadata. Allocator mechanics themselves belong to test_arena.

native_pool_workers.desc:
Both pool accessors at PC_WORKER_COUNT=2. Slot resolution is unobservable in a single-worker
build - pc_worker_self() is an inline compile-time 0 there, so a test cannot present any other
identity and every borrow lands on slot 0 whatever the accessor does. Only here does the id
become a real per-task read, so this is the only env in which a worker borrowing from its OWN
slot, and a caller that is not a server worker landing on the ghost instead of colliding with
worker 0, are distinguishable from each other.

native_mnt.desc:
Mounted storage (server/filesystem/mnt) - the backend vtable and its built-in RAM backend,
host-tested through that backend (the Arduino FS backend is board-layer and HW-verified).
Files, directories, stat, and the readdir cursor. Pure, no heap.

native_swar.desc:
Lane math (shared_primitives/swar.h): one 32-bit word as four byte lanes. has-zero across
every lane, the guard-bit range compares the base64 decoder classifies with, and the bounded
NUL scan diffed against strnlen at every length, NUL position, and alignment.
